source.title: Find Minimum Time to Reach Last Room I

teaching.hint: Can arriving at a room earlier ever make a later route through it worse, given that waiting is allowed?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: The earliest arrival at a room dominates later arrivals because one may wait; a move to a neighbor at time `t` arrives at `max(t, opening)+1`.
solution_outline.approach: Maintain earliest known arrival times and expand the room with smallest current arrival time, relaxing each side-adjacent neighbor using its opening time.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: A finalized room has its true earliest arrival; pending estimates are costs of legal routes found so far.
solution_outline.correctness: The transition is nondecreasing in departure time and never travels backward in time. The usual earliest-frontier argument therefore finalizes rooms in optimal arrival order.
solution_outline.pitfall: Plain BFS minimizes step count but can choose a route delayed by a late-opening room.

common_wrong_turns: Use BFS by number of moves
Add the opening time instead of waiting until it
source_fidelity_notes: Clarifies that entry waits before the one-second move, matching source examples.
